statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 15 of 100 in the low band, ten points below the 25 block threshold, while stress stays extreme at 82 and confidence is high at 87.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The observed cash open gave back part of the post-report advance rather than extending it, which is the evidence that carried tail down from 22 in the previous hour. The named window covers 19:00 to 21:00 UTC, the final cash hour into the 20:00 UTC close and the thin post-close futures hour before the weekend halt, where conditional tail peaks at 18 and still remains below the watch band. No slot in the forward window reaches the block threshold.
headline: The observed cash open faded rather than extended: NQ set 29,500.25 before the bell and has eased to about 29,383-29,399 by 14:16-14:30 UTC, roughly 117 points under that high while holding near a 0.9% gain, with VIX down almost 11% to 15.89 and the ten-year back to 4.932%, leaving tail at 15 in the low band against extreme stress of 82 after Michigan preliminary sentiment printed 47.8 versus 51.0 expected.
body:
Two dated releases are now verified rather than open. The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC: all items rose 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis and 3.4% over twelve months, while all items less food and energy rose 0.3% on the month and 2.4% over the year, with gasoline accounting for more than a third of the monthly increase. The University of Michigan preliminary September survey followed at 14:00 UTC and came in at 47.8 against a 51.0 consensus and a 51.7 August final, the weakest reading since May's record low, while one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.6% and the five-to-ten-year measure edged to 3.4% from 3.3%.

The decisive new evidence is the observed price path through the 13:30 UTC cash open, which the previous assessment could only frame conditionally. The opening auction did not extend the post-report leg. NQ posted its session high of 29,499.50 to 29,500.25 before the bell, traded 29,437 at 13:16 UTC, and has since eased to 29,397 to 29,399 at 14:14 to 14:16 UTC on two independent feeds and to about 29,383 by 14:30 UTC. That is a steady give-back of roughly 117 points, or 0.4%, from the high, against a session low of 29,040.50 set well before the release. Retracement is being granted, not refused, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback continuation pattern that defines the failure mode this score measures. The cash index is 29,422.90, up 1.10%, inside a 29,323.31 to 29,446.24 range.

Cross-asset evidence is constructive on the surface and still conflicted underneath. VIX is 15.89, down 10.9%, printing a 15.73 session low after a 17.71 high, so event premium is bleeding out rather than rebuilding. The ten-year is 4.932%, below its 4.944% prior close and well off the 5.005% spike the release produced. The two-year is 4.585%, up 3.5 basis points and close to its 4.611% day high, so the front end is still holding a hawkish repricing that the long end has unwound, with futures pricing roughly a 70% chance of a 25 basis point increase on 16 September. WTI is $99.65 and Brent $105.03, down 2.8% and 2.4%, relieving the oil-led pressure behind the preceding four lower closes. Semiconductors lead at SOX 11,848.97, up 2.02%, a leadership that conflicts with an index giving ground from its high.

Tail is scored at 15, down from 22. The amplifiers that argued for a higher reading an hour ago were prospective: an unobserved opening auction after four consecutive lower closes, with an aligned volatility and oil backdrop. The auction has now happened and resolved toward two-way trade. A stagflationary sentiment print landed inside this hour and did not produce a persistent directional response either, which is itself informative. Event importance, the near-record-low sentiment reading and the hike probability into next week continue to register as stress, which stays extreme at 82, rather than as tail.

Confidence is 87. Both release outcomes are confirmed, the consumer price report from the primary source and the sentiment survey from a data provider that carries the actual, current levels are corroborated across two independent price feeds plus the cash index, and volatility, both yield tenors, oil, semiconductors and the forward calendar were retrieved directly. The shared Finviz context collected at 11:51 UTC is roughly 155 minutes old and reports partial collection status with its calendar section unavailable, so it is stale under the inherited contract and carries no weight in this reading. What remains unobserved is the rest of the cash session, which is framed conditionally throughout the forward window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 14:00 UTC on 10 September to 13:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 17 with the mode mixed and holds a 14 to 19 band through that afternoon, recording event/whipsaw at 19 and 18 in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots around the previous cash close. The overnight hours from 22:00 UTC normalised into an 11 to 15 band, the quietest stretch of the window. From 06:00 UTC the mode turned trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13, 14, 15 and 14 as the overnight advance extended, stalled and was bought back. The final two slots lift to 21 and 22 with the mode event/whipsaw: the first covers the 12:30 UTC consumer price release before its outcome could be verified, the second the pre-open hour ahead of an unobserved cash open. Stress never left the extreme band, running 81 to 88, while confidence held 84 to 89 until the release hour, where it fell to 70 and then recovered to 80.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the remainder of the 11 September cash session and then spends its last seventeen slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 15 in the current slot, which now contains an observed rather than a hypothetical cash open, and eases through 15, 14 and 13 into the midday lull on the assumption that volatility decay continues and retracements keep being granted. It lifts a point across the 18:00 UTC budget statement and peaks at 18 in the 19:00 UTC final cash hour, where closing-auction and weekly-expiry flow concentrate on the Friday before a rate-decision week, then eases to 15 in the thin post-close futures hour. Every slot maps to EA_ON and none reaches the watch band, let alone the block threshold. From the 21:00 UTC halt the score collapses to 7 and then to a 5 to 6 floor, which represents weekend gap risk carried into the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen rather than any intraday mechanism, since the mean-reversion failure mode being scored cannot occur while the market is closed. Stress decays from extreme through high and elevated into the moderate band across the closure, and confidence drifts from 87 to 63 on assessment age alone.
